angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 1,962,570 km at 20.34 pc = 1.29 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 104887: distance 20.342 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.008), at which the luminosity and radius hold (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 20.342 +/- 0.163 pc; Gaia DR3 gives this source no parallax (a two-parameter solution)
radiusSource: Radius 2.821 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 104887: radius 2.821 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 10.659 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.092) and temperature (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 1,962,570 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 6214 +/- 286 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 104887: effective temperature 6214 +/- 286 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.256) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 104887: effective temperature 6214 +/- 286 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.256) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's measured spectrum (Kharitonov, Tereshchenko & Knyazeva (1988), Spectrophotometric Catalogue of Stars (Alma-Ata), record 984) (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
